blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards inherits whatever its verifier gets wrong. Outside mathematics and code the verifier is a proxy, a rubric, a learned judge or a hand-written checker, and its distance from the true objective is never measured, so a rising reward cannot be told apart from a hack. We build a setting where the true reward is exactly computable at the process level: executable authorization policies over 124,416 contexts admit an oracle that lists every minimal sufficient reason for every decision. We compile these policies into exact process rewards, degrade the verifier along seven realistic axes (outcome-only, sufficiency, recall-only, extraction noise, coarse taxonomy, stale policy, LLM judge), and train against each while the exact verifier scores every rollout. Four phenotypes appear. Optimistic verifiers are hacked by padding: the sufficiency proxy ends at 0.940 while true faithfulness falls from 0.731 to 0.667 on 96 held-out episodes. Outcome-only verifiers saturate and stop teaching, noise dilutes, and ranking-preserving gaps do no harm. A model-free audit of the verifier, its selection error and gap sign, together with a short saturation pilot, anticipates which phenotype a run will produce. Across nine configurations spanning two frameworks, two model vendors, two adapter sizes, three precisions, two initialisations and two seeds, the phenotypes recur, sufficiency damage is positive in all 10 replication cells and beyond two standard errors in 7, and optimistic gaps remain the steeper branch. The damage magnitude does not replicate, and five pre-registered attempts to explain it are reported as they fell. We release the testbed, the training instrumentation, and 14 real public policies (Cedar, OPA, Gatekeeper) ported to executable oracles.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR), where a program
checks each answer and returns the reward, has driven the recent
progress of reasoning models. In mathematics and code the verifier is exact.
Nearly everywhere else it is a
proxy, a rubric ( Gunjal et al., 2026 ) , a reference-derived signal ( Jiang et al., 2026 ) , a learned judge or a hand-built checker. Reward hacking,
a policy raising its trained reward while the true objective
falls, is studied intensively ( Amodei et al., 2016 ; Skalse et al., 2022 ; Gao et al., 2023 ; Pan et al., 2022 ; Khalifa et al., 2026 ; Wong et al., 2026 ; Helff et al., 2026 ) .
Recent work argues that noisy verifiers may be tolerable ( Plesner et al., 2026 ) , and other work shows that systematic verifier
errors shape outcomes in ways an error rate does not predict ( Egashira et al., 2026 ) . All of this work reads hacking off downstream evaluations, probes,
held-out suites or anecdote, because the true reward is unavailable for the
individual rollout, the sampled output where the behaviour arises.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
The successes of RLVR in
mathematics and code ( Shao et al., 2024 ) rest on verifiers that are
exact by construction. Extending it elsewhere has produced a family of proxy
verifiers, from rubric-based rewards ( Gunjal et al., 2026 ) and
reference-derived signal chains ( Jiang et al., 2026 ) to empirical arguments that
noisy verifiers are tolerable up to double-digit error rates ( Plesner et al., 2026 ) . Ray (2026) fuzz verifiers for exploitable bugs before
training, and, closest to us, Egashira et al. (2026) inject systematic verification errors on arithmetic and find that outcomes
range from delay to collapse in a way the overall error rate does not
predict. Mitsuhashi et al. (2026) inject random false positives and
false negatives on GSM8K and find false negatives the more damaging. All of
these must treat the verifier as given, because in their domains no
independent measurement of its distance from truth exists. Here the
verifier’s gap is itself the measured quantity. That answers the negative
result of Egashira et al. with a positive one, since damage is
predicted by selection error weighted by update flow (§ 6.1 ), and
accounts for the sign asymmetry: pessimistic noise damages in both studies,
while an optimistic verifier damages more per unit of corruption
(§ 6.1 ). The noise-tolerance claims pass our test only
conditionally, on reward granularity and on optimizer robustness
(§ 6 ).

a named property of the verifier. The starvation phenotype we

Process reward models ( Lightman et al., 2024 ) are learned and inherit judge noise, and step-level faithfulness rewards ( Gui et al., 2026 ) rely on evidence-support judges. Yuan et al. (2026) convert symbolic oracles into dense process rewards and note the
dependence on oracle quality without studying it. We study exactly that
dependence, with an oracle that is perfect and degraded by construction. Ferreira et al. (2026) add a causal-attribution signal to the
reward model after showing that preference optimisation erodes explanation
faithfulness, and Hase and Potts (2026) reward chains of thought that let a
simulator predict counterfactual outputs. Both measure faithfulness against
the model’s own behaviour, whereas our oracle scores it against the decision
function’s true reasons. Formal explainable AI (XAI) provides exact attribution for white-box
functions through abductive minimal sufficient reasons ( Shih et al., 2018 ; Ignatiev et al., 2019 ) , and GlassGate ( V, 2026 ) used it to show that frontier models’ free-form
decision explanations are causally imprecise regardless of scale. We turn
that oracle from an evaluation device into a training-time instrument.

blocks.en:

policies, first as a transfer test and then as a training domain. Models
trained only on synthetic gates must explain decisions of real,
held-out policies whose schemas they have never seen

aggregate F 1 F_{1} of 0.779 is the highest in the table, because

model’s damage survived domain shift, and the aggregate score hid it.

blocks.en: 9 Recommendations
blocks.zh: 9 建议

blocks.en:
Within the scope tested here (§ 10 ), our results support
four recommendations. Audit a process verifier’s selection error on a probe
grid before training against it. In our grids it predicted the phenotype
where reward accuracy did not, and it needs no policy model. Read the sign
too: optimistic verifiers were hacked and pessimistic ones only diluted, so
bias pessimistic when forced to choose. Do not train a process objective on
an outcome-only signal, which is blind to reasons and, once saturated,
silent. Give sufficiency- and recall-style rewards a precision term, since
alone they reward padding. An LLM judge can be used once its rankings pass a
held-out exact audit, as the one judge we trained against did.

blocks.en: Broader Impact Statement

blocks.en:
This work studies failure modes of reward verifiers using synthetic policy
gates and public, permissively licensed policy corpora. No human subjects,
personal data or proprietary data are involved. Understanding how proxy
rewards are hacked could in principle inform adversaries, but the attacks
demonstrated (padding, saturation exploitation) are already folklore. The
work contributes a defence, an audit that detects a dangerous verifier before
it is trained against.

blocks.en:
Each public policy (Table 4 ) is ported by mapping every Cedar ( Cutler et al., 2024 ) permit or forbid clause, or Rego violation rule ( Open Policy Agent, 2026 ; OPA Gatekeeper, 2026 ) , to one antecedent over categorical features. Entity-relationship conditions become boolean
features, and numeric, regex and datetime conditions are pre-bucketed into
feature values. Decision semantics are preserved exactly under DenyOverrides (default deny, permits allow, forbids override) or
admission style (empty permit plus violation forbids). Every abstraction is
recorded in a per-policy omitted field, and every port was
validated by exhaustive enumeration against the gate plus hand-traced sanity
contexts against the original source semantics, three or more per policy,
all matching. Full machine-readable specs with provenance (repository, path,
license, block rate) ship in the artifact, and all sources are Apache-2.0.
The per-policy abstraction record below is generated verbatim from those omitted fields.

blocks.en: cedar-photoapp ( cedar-policy/cedar-examples : cedar-policy-language-in-action/PhotoApp/photoapp.cedar , Apache-2.0). The scope condition `resource in PhotoApp::Application::”PhotoApp”` in every policy treated as always-true (all Photos are in the Application per the entity store). `resource has subjects && resource.subjects.contains(principal)` in @id(’Photo.subjects’) bucketed into is_subject. `context has judgingSession && context.judgingSession == true` in @id(’PhotoJudge’) bucketed into judging_session (absent attribute to no). The instance policies @id(’DoeFamily’) (DoeFamily members on Album DoePhotos) and @id(’JaneVacation’) (JohnDoe on Album JaneVacation) merged into one relationship boolean album_grant (permits are disjunctive, so merging preserves decisions). @id(’Photo.owner’)’s explicit action list is all three schema actions, so the conjunct is dropped as vacuous. Labels is a Set<String>, so label_private/label_contest are independent booleans. cedar-streaming-service ( cedar-policy/cedar-examples : cedar-example-use-cases/streaming_service/policies.cedar , Apache-2.0). All datetime arithmetic bucketed: now-vs-resource.releaseDate in @id(’subscriber-content-access/show’) and @id(’early-access-show’) to time_window (meaningful only for shows; Movie has no releaseDate, so the value is a don’t-care never consulted for movies). The conjunction resource.isOscarNominated && 2025-02-02T19:00-0500 <= now < 2025-03-02T19:00-0500 in @id(’rent-buy-oscar-movie’) to single boolean oscar_promo (a 4th ’oscar_window’ time_window value was rejected: shows at Oscars-window times still have a definite release relation, so that enum would create ill-defined contexts and break exactness). The toTime()/localTimeOffset computation in the unless-clause of @id(’forbid-bedtime-watch-kid-profile’) to is_bedtime (yes iff local time outside 06:00-21:00). FreeMember/Subscriber entity types and subscription.tier merged into 3-valued membership (FreeMember has no tier or profile; no rule consults profile_is_kid for free members). The @id(’subscriber-content-access/show’) unless-clause (A && B) split into two permits by De Morgan (not-early OR after-release). Needs_rent_or_buy / is_oscar_nominated are Movie-only and is_early_access is Show-only attributes kept as global features (don’t-cares for the other type). cedar-tags-n-roles ( cedar-policy/cedar-examples : cedar-example-use-cases/tags_n_roles/policies.cedar , Apache-2.0). Principals holding multiple roles simultaneously (entity Joe is in both Role-A and Role-B with different tag sets; Cedar’s decision is the disjunction over per-role policies), each context models the evaluation for a single role membership, which is exact for single-role principals. The guard `principal.allowedTagsForRole has ”Role-X”` repeated in every when-clause of @id(’Role-A policy’)/@id(’Role-B policy’) is folded into the match enums (a missing role record maps every dimension to not_covered, which is a consistent assignment). Per-dimension set logic bucketed into 3-valued enums: principal_all = the user’s role record lacks the tag OR its values contain ’ALL’ (user-side wildcard, matches any resource). Covered = resource lacks the tag, resource values contain ’ALL’, or user values are a superset of resource values (containsAll). Not_covered = the when-clause for that dimension is false. The Role-A action conjunct is kept explicit even though Role-A Actions contains all three schema actions. cedar-tax-preparer ( cedar-policy/cedar-examples : cedar-example-use-cases/tax_preparer/policies.cedar , Apache-2.0). The only action is viewDocument, so no action feature. Rule 1a’s assigned_orgs.contains({organization: resource.owner.organization, serviceline: resource.serviceline, location: resource.location}) set-of-records containment bucketed into assignment_covers_doc. The organization/serviceline/doc_location document descriptors are kept for realism but are decision-irrelevant (only the tuple-match boolean is consulted, since a professional may hold several assigned_orgs tuples). The @id(’adhoc-access’) template and its `linked` instantiation (link_id AliceView: Alice to Document DEF) generalized to the boolean adhoc_grant permit. Rule 2’s context.consent record split into consent_from_owner (consent.client == resource.owner) and consent_covers_location (team_region_list.contains(principal.location)). Rule 2’s `unless (A && B)` becomes two forbids (not-A; not-B). gk-block-endpoint-edit ( open-policy-agent/gatekeeper-library : library/general/block-endpoint-edit-default-role/template.yaml , Apache-2.0). Context is a single (role, policy-rule, verb) grounding of the rego’s iteration over rules[_], resources[_], verbs[_]. The three hasEditVerb helper bodies collapse into the value set {create,patch,update}. Exact string match on metadata.name ’system:aggregate-to-edit’ bucketed into role_name. Object_kind and has_autoupdate_annotation are faithful distractors, the rego never inspects kind (ClusterRole scoping is in the Constraint match) and the rbac.authorization.kubernetes.io/autoupdate annotation appears only in the advisory violation message, never in a condition. gk-container-limits ( open-policy-agent/gatekeeper-library : library/general/containerlimits/template.yaml , Apache-2.0). Parameters instantiated to cpu=’2’, memory=’1Gi’ (both finite, so the cpu != ’-1’ disable-guards are always satisfied). Canonify_cpu/canonify_mem numeric parsing and the > max comparisons are pre-bucketed into cpu_limit/mem_limit values (under_max/over_max/unparseable, unset = key absent or ”). The two rego rules ’not container.resources’ and ’not container.resources.limits’ merge into the has_limits=none bucket. The two field-wrapper violation rules (containers/initContainers) are represented by leaving container_field unconstrained in every forbid. ExemptImages prefix matching bucketed into exempt_image. Coherence: has_limits=none implies cpu/mem unset, partial implies exactly one unset, present implies neither unset, decisions on incoherent product contexts have no rego ground truth. Ephemeral containers not checked by the template (field cannot be set). gk-disallowed-tags ( open-policy-agent/gatekeeper-library : library/general/disallowedtags/template.yaml , Apache-2.0). Parameters instantiated to tags=[’latest’]. Suffix matching (strings.any_suffix_match against ’:latest’) and the split-by-’/’ untagged check are pre-bucketed into image_tag: none = no colon in last segment, latest = ends with ’:latest’, pinned = any other tag, digest = @sha256:… references which trip neither rule (colon present, suffix differs) and are admitted. The three input_containers union rules are represented by leaving container_field unconstrained in both forbids. ExemptImages prefix matching bucketed into exempt_image. Image_registry is a faithful distractor, split(image, ’/’) means even a registry port colon (registry:5000/app) never masks an untagged image. gk-psp-hostnet ( open-policy-agent/gatekeeper-library : library/pod-security-policy/host-network-ports/template.yaml , Apache-2.0). Numeric min/max range bucketed into host_port. Host_port=none covers no ports and ports without hostPort. Single container with a single port modeled (source iterates all containers x ports). ExemptImages prefix matching bucketed to exempt_image (applies only to the port check, matching the rego). UPDATE operations bypass all checks (hostNetwork is immutable). CEL variant’s ports.all() differs from the rego’s any-port semantics, the Rego engine is ported. gk-psp-seccomp ( open-policy-agent/gatekeeper-library : library/pod-security-policy/seccomp/template.yaml , Apache-2.0). Allowlist instantiations: wildcard=[’*’] (short-circuits all checks including exemption), runtime_default_only=[’runtime/default’], runtime_and_localhost=[’runtime/default’,’localhost/allowed.json’] (exact file match, no localhost/* wildcard). Resolved_profile collapses the four resolution locations (pod/container annotation, pod/container securityContext), location affects only the message. Docker_default models the annotation-scheme string ’docker/default’ (securityContext RuntimeDefault canonicalizes to an allowed variant and cannot produce it). SecurityContext-scheme parameter translation (RuntimeDefault/Localhost/allowedLocalhostFiles) folded into the same canonical allowlists. Single container modeled. No update exclusion exists in this template. CEL engine variant is decision-equivalent. gk-psp-users ( open-policy-agent/gatekeeper-library : library/pod-security-policy/users/template.yaml , Apache-2.0). RunAsGroup and supplementalGroups families dropped to stay <=6 features (same accept_value logic as fsGroup; supplementalGroups additionally iterates array values). Provided_user=root means uid 0 and is assumed outside the MustRunAs ranges. The runAsNonRoot=true escape hatch (runAsUser unset but runAsNonRoot set gives no NonRoot violation) is not modeled, unset means neither field is set. Container/pod-level securityContext precedence collapsed into the single provided value. Single container modeled (containers/initContainers/ephemeralContainers union). ExemptImages prefix matching bucketed to exempt_image. gk-required-labels ( open-policy-agent/gatekeeper-library : library/general/requiredlabels/template.yaml , Apache-2.0). blocks.en:
The policy is Qwen3-4B (4-bit, MLX) with LoRA adapters (7.34M trainable parameters),
initialised from a teacher-distilled SFT adapter. Training uses policy gradient with
group-relative advantage, group 8, temperature 0.8, at most 220 new tokens,
Adam at learning rate 5 × 10 − 6 5\times 10^{-6} , global-norm gradient clipping at 1.0,
per-completion gradient accumulation, 150 steps, and greedy held-out evals
every 25 steps on 8 episodes during training. Steps with zero group variance
are logged and skipped with no update. Seeds are 11 and 12.
Table 5 lists the full configuration of both the final
recipe and the initial recipe whose fragility is analysed in
Appendix E . Both are archived as config.json alongside
every run’s per-step logs and terminal adapters. One run takes about 75
minutes of wall-clock (the LLM-judge cell is slower, because its extraction
API calls dominate), and the full grid takes about 30 hours.

blocks.en:
The replication trainer is a line-by-line port of
the MLX loop to PyTorch with PEFT. It keeps the group size, learning rate, clipping, temperature, token budget,

circuit breaker on 25 consecutive identical groups. Adapters carry a base-model marker that the loader checks, after one
run silently loaded a Phi adapter onto Qwen through a name collision. The
matched adapter targets every attention and MLP projection in the last 16
layers with rank 8 and scale 20, which is the MLX adapter exactly. A run on
a T4 takes about 3.5 hours for 150 steps.

blocks.en: Appendix E Optimizer Fragility
blocks.zh: 附录E 优化脆弱性

blocks.en:
Two negative results shaped the recipe. First, an off-the-shelf MLX GRPO
implementation produced checkpoints byte-identical to initialisation, a
silent zero-gradient no-op. The released trainer is a transparent REINFORCE
loop with group-relative advantage, the GRPO core at on-policy single-step,
with a first-step proof-of-life assertion on gradient norms and weight
deltas. Second, the initial recipe (learning rate 10 − 5 10^{-5} , group 4, no
clipping) was seed-unstable. The exact-reward control itself collapsed on
one seed to a terminal true reward of 0.401 0.401 , and under it the
noise ( ε = .15 ) (\varepsilon{=}.15) cell collapsed to 0.083 0.083 , against
0.678 under the final recipe. The two old-recipe figures in
this paragraph are in-training 8-episode evaluations. Those runs predate the
terminal re-scoring and saved no adapter to re-score, so they are not
comparable at the third decimal with the n = 96 n=96 numbers used
everywhere else. The comparison they support is a collapse against a stable
level, which no measurement noise explains. Figure 5 shows
both comparisons step by step: the noise cell decays roughly monotonically to
collapse under the fragile optimizer and holds a diluted level under the
clipped one, and the exact control survives both but dips sharply mid-run
without clipping. Verifier noise and optimizer fragility therefore compound:
a gap that is benign under a stable optimizer can be catastrophic under a
fragile one. All old-recipe runs are preserved in the artifact.
blocks.zh:

The sufficiency cell does +0.033 ± \pm 0.043 of damage
with citation inflation +0.21 and 116 skipped
updates. The outcome proxy saturates at 1.000 and skips
149 updates for +0.026 of damage. Noise costs
+0.008 and the stale policy +0.017. Scored against PREREG_corpus.md , the record reads C1 met. C2 sufficiency-most-damaging met, citation inflation above 0.5 not met, outcome saturation met, stale policy harmless met, noise between them not met. C3 met (control 0.785 against the untrained base 0.759). C4 met ( β + = 0.94 \beta_{+}=0.94 against β − = 0.07 \beta_{-}=0.07 ). C5 not met (step-1 group reward 0.889, 85 of 150 control steps skipped). Because C5 is not
met, the pre-registration’s own rule applies. The corpus contributes its
audit, which transferred, and a descriptive grid in which only the identity
of the top cell (sufficiency) matches the synthetic family and every damage
is within about one standard error of zero. It does not contribute a second measurement of damage. The control’s gain over the base
(+0.026 ± \pm 0.044) is likewise directional only.
